models.name: Orc Skull Scavengers
models.appearance: A compact green orc with a pointed brown hood, short booted legs, a skull belt, a large rear sack and a cleaver in the anatomical right hand.

models.primaryMotion: Proposed scavenging trudge: alert enough to advance, but subtly pulled backward and sideways by the sack rather than marching symmetrically.
models.walk: Use short alternating steps with a modest forward chest lean. Shift the pelvis over the planted boot before lifting the opposite foot; keep each sole fixed throughout support. The free arm counterbalances while the cleaver stays outside the knee corridor.
models.run: A hurried, slightly ungainly jog with increased cadence and only a small airborne interval. The sack limits torso rotation; do not simply stretch the walking stride or swing the blade across the face.

models.turning: Use a large turning radius or several braced steps. The shield's width makes fast pivoting and planted-foot spinning inappropriate.

transitions.authoredIntent: Acceleration needs a clear preparatory compression; stopping uses a broad brace and a second collecting step. Do not drag the shield through the ground merely because older prose calls it a door.
transitions.start: Blend from exact rest over a reviewable 0.15–0.30 second interval. Select a valid first support or wing phase before translating along the route.
transitions.stop: Keep the last support foot or carried saddle relationship; finish one restrained settle. Final route-aware support selection is not implemented in the START pilot.
transitions.turn: Yaw the route carrier separately from limb joints. Use the authored turning intent and replant/ bank only after endpoint and collision review.
transitions.scrubAndReset: Evaluate from rest coordinates at every frame; no cumulative integration. Test zero time, reverse scrubbing and repeated enable/disable.

models.secondaryMotion: Leather straps and skirt lag slightly; large armor plates, horns and door boards behave as heavy rigid structures.
eventConstraints: Keep the anatomical right implement and left shield assignments. Future rig design must preserve grips, shoulder clearance and the approved equipment silhouette.

Locomotion never triggers attack, damage, armor shedding, spell, drum impact or death events automatically. Those require separate gameplay event channels.
Rest and reset must exactly restore working-copy positions and joint transforms. No accumulating per-frame rotations or vertex offsets.
Contact events are proposed per support phase; route velocity stays authoritative. Match stride/cadence to displacement before enabling in-game root motion.
reviewChecklist: Boss weight, readable forward intent, secure door control and planted feet under the broad load.

Check every support contact or wing root, every held grip, and the complete follower assembly; no floating cuffs, armor, cargo or saddle.
Check loop position AND velocity, start/stop blend, turning ownership and reset after arbitrary scrubbing.
Check silhouette, self-intersection, membrane/tissue compression, foot sliding and ground penetration. A moving preview is not geometry/contact acceptance.
Compare current part inventory against the recorded GLB before admitting any new semantic binding.

models.run: A compact armored jog with both elbows closer to the ribs. The hooks remain in a guarded carrying position rather than becoming large alternating attack swings.

transitions.authoredIntent: Start almost without upper-body preparation, but retain a visible foot push. Stop through one restrained braking step and let the hem finish moving afterward.

models.name: Gorvash, the Bone Patriarch
models.appearance: A massive green patriarch has long arms, a broad leather-clad torso, a tall open rib crown, a strapped rear throne and a segmented pale bone club.

models.primaryMotion: Proposed stately crushing advance: the body carries ceremonial loads with authority rather than the comic wobble of the younger ogre.
models.walk: Use broad deliberate steps with long full-foot support. The pelvis crosses onto the receiving leg before the trailing foot releases; shoulders remain comparatively level to support the crown and rear throne.
models.run: A committed boss charge with shortened but powerful steps and modest forward pitch. Keep the bone club controlled on its existing right side, without a full attack swing inside the locomotion loop.

cycle.runRule: Separate final run/canter/flight-acceleration clips are required. Initial speed preview can adjust cadence but cannot claim completed run mechanics.

models.massAndBalance: Heavy hips lead slow acceleration. Upper mass settles after support contact with small amplitude. Preserve empty armor, open ribs and belly-mouth anatomy; their gaps cannot close as a breathing substitute.

models.turning: Use wide stepping turns and a slower upper-body follow-through. The tall crown and throne should remain connected to their actual carriers throughout.

transitions.authoredIntent: Acceleration starts with a clear compression under the load. Braking finishes in a broad brace and one collecting step rather than a sudden motionless root.
transitions.start: Blend from exact rest over a reviewable 0.15–0.30 second interval. Select a valid first support or wing phase before translating along the route.
transitions.stop: Keep the last support foot or carried saddle relationship; finish one restrained settle. Final route-aware support selection is not implemented in the START pilot.
transitions.turn: Yaw the route carrier separately from limb joints. Use the authored turning intent and replant/ bank only after endpoint and collision review.
transitions.scrubAndReset: Evaluate from rest coordinates at every frame; no cumulative integration. Test zero time, reverse scrubbing and repeated enable/disable.

models.secondaryMotion: Leather tabs and hanging rings may settle after contact; crown ribs and club segments retain rigid structural relationships.
eventConstraints: Do not animate the rear throne as an unsupported floating object. Future rig design must maintain crown clearance, shoulders, right grip and the heavy back attachment.
Original GLB positions, indices, material assignments, UVs, source cameras and approved source images remain immutable. Runtime deformation must clone geometry before writing.
Each mesh has one owner; a connected anatomy mesh cannot be attached to two independent rigid joints. Use explicit continuous weights on a runtime clone, or author a separate reviewed rig.
Locomotion never triggers attack, damage, armor shedding, spell, drum impact or death events automatically. Those require separate gameplay event channels.
Rest and reset must exactly restore working-copy positions and joint transforms. No accumulating per-frame rotations or vertex offsets.
Contact events are proposed per support phase; route velocity stays authoritative. Match stride/cadence to displacement before enabling in-game root motion.
reviewChecklist: Readable patriarch stature, stable ceremonial loads, planted feet and convincing charge-to-stop weight.
Inspect front, both sides, rear and three-quarter motion at quarter-cycle intervals and at full speed.
Check every support contact or wing root, every held grip, and the complete follower assembly; no floating cuffs, armor, cargo or saddle.
Check loop position AND velocity, start/stop blend, turning ownership and reset after arbitrary scrubbing.
Check silhouette, self-intersection, membrane/tissue compression, foot sliding and ground penetration. A moving preview is not geometry/contact acceptance.
Compare current part inventory against the recorded GLB before admitting any new semantic binding.

models.name: Rotroot Trolls
models.appearance: The approved troll combines visible green anatomy with dense moss cowls, a bark-and-foliage chest, branched crown, curled root fists and bark-covered feet.

implementation.previewTimeEvaluation: Pure time/mode/speed/blend evaluation. Same phase gives the same pose after arbitrary seeking and reset; production start/stop envelopes remain pending.

gameplayAuthority.rule: Keep this route speed authoritative; preview cycle duration does not change gameplay velocity.

models.primaryMotion: Proposed rooted but mobile lumber: living joints drive the stride while woody masses retain their structure and foliage follows with restrained softness.
models.walk: Use short broad steps with a clear lateral weight transfer and fixed support soles. Keep knees flexed enough for the bark foot wraps, and swing the heavy root fists in small arcs outside the torso.
models.run: A forceful low lope with increased cadence and modest forward lean. Avoid stretching the connected body like rubber or opening the curled fists merely to exaggerate movement.

cycle.phaseConvention: Normalized 0..1; time in seconds; all numeric amplitudes are initial review proposals.

phaseEvents.description: Left foot receives weight with a broad sole.
Chest advances only after the left support is established.
Right foot clears with a compact recovery.
Right foot receives weight; retain a short double-support interval.
Left recovery passes the grounded leg.
Left support returns with restrained upper-body settling.

cycle.strideAndLift: Propose 0.16–0.26 hip-to-sole length travel and 0.035–0.065 lift. Increase cadence before reach; do not stretch huge feet or shorten long arms.
cycle.cadenceRule: Existing route speed governs translation. Use long walking support, with pelvis, bark and foliage responses ordered progressively over the following quarter-cycle.
cycle.runRule: Separate final run/canter/flight-acceleration clips are required. Initial speed preview can adjust cadence but cannot claim completed run mechanics.

models.massAndBalance: Heavy hips lead slow acceleration. Upper mass settles after support contact with small amplitude. Preserve empty armor, open ribs and belly-mouth anatomy; their gaps cannot close as a breathing substitute.

partOwnership.coordinateFrame: Imported glTF scene: +Y up, +Z model front, X lateral. Bounds below are literal glTF accessor coordinates.
partOwnership.method: Literal mesh inventory and conservative name-based ownership review. Fused anatomy is recorded explicitly and is not split by names.

models.turning: Redirect with several planted steps. The exposed face leads slightly while the mantle and branched crown remain seated on their approved supports.

transitions.authoredIntent: Gather weight beneath a foot before starting; braking ends in a broad brace with a brief cascade of moss settling down the back.
transitions.start: Blend from exact rest over a reviewable 0.15–0.30 second interval. Select a valid first support or wing phase before translating along the route.
transitions.stop: Keep the last support foot or carried saddle relationship; finish one restrained settle. Final route-aware support selection is not implemented in the START pilot.
transitions.turn: Yaw the route carrier separately from limb joints. Use the authored turning intent and replant/ bank only after endpoint and collision review.
transitions.scrubAndReset: Evaluate from rest coordinates at every frame; no cumulative integration. Test zero time, reverse scrubbing and repeated enable/disable.

models.secondaryMotion: Small moss clusters, temple strands and chest foliage can respond at different delays; major bark courses and branches remain comparatively rigid.
eventConstraints: Keep true fist recesses, foot wraps, open forehead and tusk roots intact. Future rig planning must map continuous anatomy and attached organic layers before any deformation work.
Original GLB positions, indices, material assignments, UVs, source cameras and approved source images remain immutable. Runtime deformation must clone geometry before writing.
Each mesh has one owner; a connected anatomy mesh cannot be attached to two independent rigid joints. Use explicit continuous weights on a runtime clone, or author a separate reviewed rig.
Locomotion never triggers attack, damage, armor shedding, spell, drum impact or death events automatically. Those require separate gameplay event channels.
Rest and reset must exactly restore working-copy positions and joint transforms. No accumulating per-frame rotations or vertex offsets.
Contact events are proposed per support phase; route velocity stays authoritative. Match stride/cadence to displacement before enabling in-game root motion.
reviewChecklist: Rooted weight without foot slip, readable curled fists and stable mantle/crown attachments rather than a vibrating leaf cloud.
Inspect front, both sides, rear and three-quarter motion at quarter-cycle intervals and at full speed.
Check every support contact or wing root, every held grip, and the complete follower assembly; no floating cuffs, armor, cargo or saddle.
Check loop position AND velocity, start/stop blend, turning ownership and reset after arbitrary scrubbing.
Check silhouette, self-intersection, membrane/tissue compression, foot sliding and ground penetration. A moving preview is not geometry/contact acceptance.
Compare current part inventory against the recorded GLB before admitting any new semantic binding.

glbInspection.nodeHierarchy: Flat authored mesh nodes under one scene root; no anatomical bone hierarchy is inferred.

models.name: Iron Ram Ogres
models.appearance: A broad green ogre is enclosed in continuous metal armor with huge curled ram horns, thick shoulder pieces, substantial boots and a square-headed right-hand hammer.

implementation.previewTimeEvaluation: Pure time/mode/speed/blend evaluation. Same phase gives the same pose after arbitrary seeking and reset; production start/stop envelopes remain pending.

gameplayAuthority.rule: Keep this route speed authoritative; preview cycle duration does not change gameplay velocity.

models.primaryMotion: Proposed armored piston-like march, with deliberate living weight underneath rigid plates rather than the loose movement of a cloth-clad troll.
models.walk: Use broad short steps, modest knee lift and an obvious support transfer over each planted boot. The pelvis can rotate slightly, but shoulder armor and horns remain comparatively steady and clear of the hammer.
models.run: A short armored rush with compact leg recovery and a stronger forward pitch. Keep the hammer head controlled close to its carrying side; do not let it scrape the floor between strides.

cycle.phaseConvention: Normalized 0..1; time in seconds; all numeric amplitudes are initial review proposals.

phaseEvents.description: Left foot receives weight with a broad sole.
Chest advances only after the left support is established.
Right foot clears with a compact recovery.
Right foot receives weight; retain a short double-support interval.
Left recovery passes the grounded leg.
Left support returns with restrained upper-body settling.

cycle.strideAndLift: Propose 0.16–0.26 hip-to-sole length travel and 0.035–0.065 lift. Increase cadence before reach; do not stretch huge feet or shorten long arms.
cycle.cadenceRule: Existing route speed governs translation. Walking holds double support longer than agile infantry. Plate settling follows body contact quickly, while straps lag slightly further.
cycle.runRule: Separate final run/canter/flight-acceleration clips are required. Initial speed preview can adjust cadence but cannot claim completed run mechanics.

models.massAndBalance: Heavy hips lead slow acceleration. Upper mass settles after support contact with small amplitude. Preserve empty armor, open ribs and belly-mouth anatomy; their gaps cannot close as a breathing substitute.

partOwnership.coordinateFrame: Imported glTF scene: +Y up, +Z model front. Literal accessor bounds are preserved; Source22 sceneLocalBounds also include each actual authored node translation.
partOwnership.method: Literal mesh inventory and conservative name-based ownership review. Fused anatomy is recorded explicitly and is not split by names.

models.turning: Use a multi-step turn to preserve balance under the broad armor. Avoid instant pivots that would drag both soles or interlock the shoulder plates.

transitions.authoredIntent: Starting loads the knees and ankles; stopping requires a visible braced placement and smaller settling step under the metal mass.
transitions.start: Blend from exact rest over a reviewable 0.15–0.30 second interval. Select a valid first support or wing phase before translating along the route.
transitions.stop: Keep the last support foot or carried saddle relationship; finish one restrained settle. Final route-aware support selection is not implemented in the START pilot.
transitions.turn: Yaw the route carrier separately from limb joints. Use the authored turning intent and replant/ bank only after endpoint and collision review.
transitions.scrubAndReset: Evaluate from rest coordinates at every frame; no cumulative integration. Test zero time, reverse scrubbing and repeated enable/disable.

models.secondaryMotion: Use only small belt, skirt and strap responses. Horns and large armor plates should not flex like rubber or continually rattle loose.
eventConstraints: Preserve the right hammer grip and continuous armor relationships. Future rig considerations must define clearance at hips, knees, elbows and shoulders before movement is attempted.
Original GLB positions, indices, material assignments, UVs, source cameras and approved source images remain immutable. Runtime deformation must clone geometry before writing.
Each mesh has one owner; a connected anatomy mesh cannot be attached to two independent rigid joints. Use explicit continuous weights on a runtime clone, or author a separate reviewed rig.
Locomotion never triggers attack, damage, armor shedding, spell, drum impact or death events automatically. Those require separate gameplay event channels.
Rest and reset must exactly restore working-copy positions and joint transforms. No accumulating per-frame rotations or vertex offsets.
Contact events are proposed per support phase; route velocity stays authoritative. Match stride/cadence to displacement before enabling in-game root motion.
reviewChecklist: Dense armored weight, solid boot contacts and clean joint gaps with the ram-horn silhouette preserved.
Inspect front, both sides, rear and three-quarter motion at quarter-cycle intervals and at full speed.
Check every support contact or wing root, every held grip, and the complete follower assembly; no floating cuffs, armor, cargo or saddle.
Check loop position AND velocity, start/stop blend, turning ownership and reset after arbitrary scrubbing.
Check silhouette, self-intersection, membrane/tissue compression, foot sliding and ground penetration. A moving preview is not geometry/contact acceptance.
Compare current part inventory against the recorded GLB before admitting any new semantic binding.

models.name: Shard-Soul Orc Warlocks
models.appearance: A pale cyan hooded warlock has visible feet and hands, a dark angular robe, a tall staff and three floating mask fragments around the head.

implementation.previewTimeEvaluation: Pure time/mode/speed/blend evaluation. Same phase gives the same pose after arbitrary seeking and reset; production start/stop envelopes remain pending.

gameplayAuthority.rule: Keep this route speed authoritative; preview cycle duration does not change gameplay velocity.

models.primaryMotion: Proposed quiet spectral procession. Floating masks do not by themselves establish that the entire approved character should fly or lose grounded footwork.
models.walk: Use small smooth steps beneath the robe with very little head bob. Retain genuine planted feet during support, while the pelvis advances steadily and the right staff hand keeps a controlled vertical carrying line.
models.run: A restrained hurried advance rather than an athletic sprint: slightly shorter support, a modest forward lean and carefully recovered feet below the robe. A separate hovering mode would require a later explicit design decision.

cycle.phaseConvention: Normalized 0..1; time in seconds; all numeric amplitudes are initial review proposals.

phaseEvents.description: Left foot receives weight with a broad sole.
Chest advances only after the left support is established.
Right foot clears with a compact recovery.
Right foot receives weight; retain a short double-support interval.
Left recovery passes the grounded leg.
Left support returns with restrained upper-body settling.

cycle.strideAndLift: Propose 0.16–0.26 hip-to-sole length travel and 0.035–0.065 lift. Increase cadence before reach; do not stretch huge feet or shorten long arms.
cycle.cadenceRule: Existing route speed governs translation. Foot contacts remain alternating; mask drift spans several strides rather than matching every contact. Robe motion trails by a small fraction-cycle.
cycle.runRule: Separate final run/canter/flight-acceleration clips are required. Initial speed preview can adjust cadence but cannot claim completed run mechanics.

models.massAndBalance: Heavy hips lead slow acceleration. Upper mass settles after support contact with small amplitude. Preserve empty armor, open ribs and belly-mouth anatomy; their gaps cannot close as a breathing substitute.

models.turning: Lead with gaze and staff orientation, then take small collecting steps. The mask formation follows the head without cutting through the hood or staff.

transitions.authoredIntent: Begin with a subtle weight transfer and stop without an abrupt robe freeze. Keep magical appearance changes separate from locomotion support.
transitions.start: Blend from exact rest over a reviewable 0.15–0.30 second interval. Select a valid first support or wing phase before translating along the route.
transitions.stop: Keep the last support foot or carried saddle relationship; finish one restrained settle. Final route-aware support selection is not implemented in the START pilot.
transitions.turn: Yaw the route carrier separately from limb joints. Use the authored turning intent and replant/ bank only after endpoint and collision review.
transitions.scrubAndReset: Evaluate from rest coordinates at every frame; no cumulative integration. Test zero time, reverse scrubbing and repeated enable/disable.

models.secondaryMotion: Give the three mask pieces a slow differentiated drift and the robe hem a restrained trailing response; preserve the hollow visual spaces.
eventConstraints: Do not close translucent gaps or invent flight from immunity prose. Future rig needs concern staff grip, robe clearance and independent mask controls only.
Original GLB positions, indices, material assignments, UVs, source cameras and approved source images remain immutable. Runtime deformation must clone geometry before writing.
Each mesh has one owner; a connected anatomy mesh cannot be attached to two independent rigid joints. Use explicit continuous weights on a runtime clone, or author a separate reviewed rig.
Locomotion never triggers attack, damage, armor shedding, spell, drum impact or death events automatically. Those require separate gameplay event channels.
Rest and reset must exactly restore working-copy positions and joint transforms. No accumulating per-frame rotations or vertex offsets.
Contact events are proposed per support phase; route velocity stays authoritative. Match stride/cadence to displacement before enabling in-game root motion.
reviewChecklist: An eerie smooth silhouette with credible feet, stable staff carriage and clearly separate mask fragments.
Inspect front, both sides, rear and three-quarter motion at quarter-cycle intervals and at full speed.
Check every support contact or wing root, every held grip, and the complete follower assembly; no floating cuffs, armor, cargo or saddle.
Check loop position AND velocity, start/stop blend, turning ownership and reset after arbitrary scrubbing.
Check silhouette, self-intersection, membrane/tissue compression, foot sliding and ground penetration. A moving preview is not geometry/contact acceptance.
Compare current part inventory against the recorded GLB before admitting any new semantic binding.

models.turning: Use differential foot placements and a collecting step. The pilot's head may anticipate the turn, but the whole machine cannot rotate above unmoving planted feet.

transitions.authoredIntent: Start with a visible mechanical load-taking compression. Braking includes a broad final placement and a short pilot response after the frame stops.
transitions.start: Blend from exact rest over a reviewable 0.15–0.30 second interval. Select a valid first support or wing phase before translating along the route.
transitions.stop: Keep the last support foot or carried saddle relationship; finish one restrained settle. Final route-aware support selection is not implemented in the START pilot.
transitions.turn: Yaw the route carrier separately from limb joints. Use the authored turning intent and replant/ bank only after endpoint and collision review.
transitions.scrubAndReset: Evaluate from rest coordinates at every frame; no cumulative integration. Test zero time, reverse scrubbing and repeated enable/disable.

models.secondaryMotion: Permit tiny linkage and cockpit vibration; chest armor closures belong to a separate proposed reactive state, not constant walking chatter.
eventConstraints: Keep the pilot seated within the frame and preserve all approved armor plates. Future rig work must identify actual mechanical pivots and rigid part groups before animation implementation.
Original GLB positions, indices, material assignments, UVs, source cameras and approved source images remain immutable. Runtime deformation must clone geometry before writing.
Each mesh has one owner; a connected anatomy mesh cannot be attached to two independent rigid joints. Use explicit continuous weights on a runtime clone, or author a separate reviewed rig.
Locomotion never triggers attack, damage, armor shedding, spell, drum impact or death events automatically. Those require separate gameplay event channels.
Rest and reset must exactly restore working-copy positions and joint transforms. No accumulating per-frame rotations or vertex offsets.
Contact events are proposed per support phase; route velocity stays authoritative. Match stride/cadence to displacement before enabling in-game root motion.
reviewChecklist: Mechanical weight, no sliding soles, readable pilot scale and joint motion that does not bend rigid metal.
Inspect front, both sides, rear and three-quarter motion at quarter-cycle intervals and at full speed.
Check every support contact or wing root, every held grip, and the complete follower assembly; no floating cuffs, armor, cargo or saddle.
Check loop position AND velocity, start/stop blend, turning ownership and reset after arbitrary scrubbing.
Check silhouette, self-intersection, membrane/tissue compression, foot sliding and ground penetration. A moving preview is not geometry/contact acceptance.
Compare current part inventory against the recorded GLB before admitting any new semantic binding.

models.name: Iron Bat Orc Riders
models.category: Armored bat flight with crossbow rider
models.appearance: A compact helmeted rider holds a crossbow above a heavily plated bat with a metal face, broad angular purple wings and reinforced joints.

implementation.previewTimeEvaluation: Pure time/mode/speed/blend evaluation. Same phase gives the same pose after arbitrary seeking and reset; production start/stop envelopes remain pending.

gameplayAuthority.rule: Keep this route speed authoritative; preview cycle duration does not change gameplay velocity.

models.primaryMotion: Proposed weighty sustained flight with slower-looking, purposeful wing effort and a rider whose weapon remains independently readable.
models.flight: Resolve the rider's short bent legs and secure seat before testing wing extremes. Use shoulder-led power strokes with comparatively small flex in armored joint regions, then a deliberate recovery. Let the bat torso respond to lift while the rider absorbs motion through the seat, maintaining right trigger hand and left forward-stock support.

cycle.phaseConvention: Normalized 0..1; time in seconds; all numeric amplitudes are initial review proposals.

phaseEvents.description: Shoulder reaches the upper reversal; avoid an instantaneous direction snap.
Broad downstroke accelerates from shoulder through elbow.
Lower reversal; distal fingers lag the shoulder.
Recovery upstroke slightly folds the outer field.
Shoulder opens toward the next downstroke.
Wing position and velocity loop continuously.

cycle.strideAndLift: No ground stride in the primary flight clip. Initial shoulder stroke 18–30 degrees total around the actual lateral joint; elbow/finger response 5–12 degrees after 0.06–0.10 cycle. These are review proposals, not aerodynamic measurements.
cycle.cadenceRule: Existing route speed governs translation. Keep a clear power/recovery contrast, with a brief top-of-stroke gathering phase and rider response delayed approximately one eighth-cycle.
cycle.runRule: Separate final run/canter/flight-acceleration clips are required. Initial speed preview can adjust cadence but cannot claim completed run mechanics.

models.massAndBalance: The biological trunk carries saddle and rider. Wing force produces restrained trunk response; rider hips remain seated and short bent knees stay forward of the wing roots. Collar support remains underneath the neck, never on top of the head.

partOwnership.coordinateFrame: Imported glTF scene: +Y up, +Z model front, X lateral. Bounds below are literal glTF accessor coordinates.
partOwnership.method: Literal mesh inventory and conservative name-based ownership review. Fused anatomy is recorded explicitly and is not split by names.

models.turning: Bank the cockpit slightly, bias the outside stroke, then countersteer smoothly before returning level. Avoid instant yaw of the heavy hull.

transitions.authoredIntent: Open wings before increasing stroke excursion. When slowing, level the cockpit before reducing beats; the underside is not a walking undercarriage.
transitions.start: Blend from exact rest over a reviewable 0.15–0.30 second interval. Select a valid first support or wing phase before translating along the route.
transitions.stop: Keep the last support foot or carried saddle relationship; finish one restrained settle. Final route-aware support selection is not implemented in the START pilot.
transitions.turn: Yaw the route carrier separately from limb joints. Use the authored turning intent and replant/ bank only after endpoint and collision review.
transitions.scrubAndReset: Evaluate from rest coordinates at every frame; no cumulative integration. Test zero time, reverse scrubbing and repeated enable/disable.

models.secondaryMotion: Ears and loose equipment lag gently. Keep the crossbow rail straight, right hand at the trigger and left hand at forward support.
eventConstraints: Future controls must separate hull, hinges and pilot. Preserve twelve protective plates as fitted hardware; normal locomotion must not trigger their hit response. Check strokes against cockpit corners, rein controls and the weapon.
Original GLB positions, indices, material assignments, UVs, source cameras and approved source images remain immutable. Runtime deformation must clone geometry before writing.
Each mesh has one owner; a connected anatomy mesh cannot be attached to two independent rigid joints. Use explicit continuous weights on a runtime clone, or author a separate reviewed rig.
Locomotion never triggers attack, damage, armor shedding, spell, drum impact or death events automatically. Those require separate gameplay event channels.
Rest and reset must exactly restore working-copy positions and joint transforms. No accumulating per-frame rotations or vertex offsets.
Short rider legs and bent knees remain forward of the wing roots. Verify the collar/support path underneath the neck in side and underside views.
The rider hand, held grip and weapon remain a single owned chain; reins require constrained endpoints or a documented rest-preserving prototype.
reviewChecklist: Approve readable hinge rotation, seated contact and fabric that never passes through the cockpit or crossbow.
Inspect front, both sides, rear and three-quarter motion at quarter-cycle intervals and at full speed.
Check every support contact or wing root, every held grip, and the complete follower assembly; no floating cuffs, armor, cargo or saddle.
Check loop position AND velocity, start/stop blend, turning ownership and reset after arbitrary scrubbing.
Check silhouette, self-intersection, membrane/tissue compression, foot sliding and ground penetration. A moving preview is not geometry/contact acceptance.
Compare current part inventory against the recorded GLB before admitting any new semantic binding.

models.name: Prismatic Bat Tricksters
models.appearance: A narrow violet bat carries a hooded rider, dagger and cyan faceted crystals; revised bent legs and saddle sit ahead of wing roots.

implementation.previewTimeEvaluation: Pure time/mode/speed/blend evaluation. Same phase gives the same pose after arbitrary seeking and reset; production start/stop envelopes remain pending.

gameplayAuthority.rule: Keep this route speed authoritative; preview cycle duration does not change gameplay velocity.

models.primaryMotion: Use economical, quick bat strokes with a relatively quiet rider, making the small silhouette agile without specifying travel speed.
models.flight: Rotate shoulders, then elbows and outer wing supports. Membranes follow with limited recovery folding. Keep the head steadier than shoulders, hind feet tucked, and insert occasional short glides after active beats.

cycle.phaseConvention: Normalized 0..1; time in seconds; all numeric amplitudes are initial review proposals.

phaseEvents.description: Shoulder reaches the upper reversal; avoid an instantaneous direction snap.
Broad downstroke accelerates from shoulder through elbow.
Lower reversal; distal fingers lag the shoulder.
Recovery upstroke slightly folds the outer field.
Shoulder opens toward the next downstroke.
Wing position and velocity loop continuously.

cycle.strideAndLift: No ground stride in the primary flight clip. Initial shoulder stroke 18–30 degrees total around the actual lateral joint; elbow/finger response 5–12 degrees after 0.06–0.10 cycle. These are review proposals, not aerodynamic measurements.
cycle.cadenceRule: Keep current data route speed 2.50; derive cadence from displacement. Place the compact downstroke in the first half-cycle; delay rider heave slightly behind the bat's torso.
cycle.runRule: Separate final run/canter/flight-acceleration clips are required. Initial speed preview can adjust cadence but cannot claim completed run mechanics.

models.massAndBalance: The biological trunk carries saddle and rider. Wing force produces restrained trunk response; rider hips remain seated and short bent knees stay forward of the wing roots. Collar support remains underneath the neck, never on top of the head.

models.turning: Start with a neck glance, then a broad bank and outside-wing extension. Minimal rider counterlean keeps crown and axe readable.

transitions.authoredIntent: Prepare takeoff with a hind-foot brace before wing drive. Landing reaches feet beneath the mass, followed by prolonged settling of mount and rider.
transitions.start: Blend from exact rest over a reviewable 0.15–0.30 second interval. Select a valid first support or wing phase before translating along the route.
transitions.stop: Keep the last support foot or carried saddle relationship; finish one restrained settle. Final route-aware support selection is not implemented in the START pilot.
transitions.turn: Yaw the route carrier separately from limb joints. Use the authored turning intent and replant/ bank only after endpoint and collision review.
transitions.scrubAndReset: Evaluate from rest coordinates at every frame; no cumulative integration. Test zero time, reverse scrubbing and repeated enable/disable.

models.secondaryMotion: Tabard and ornaments respond with small delays. Axe inertia affects shoulder balance but never pulls the hand from its actual grip.
eventConstraints: Keep short knees ahead of wings and clear of four horn roots. Collar remains beneath the neck, not around the jaw. Future limits must preserve actual wing forelimbs, saddle, reins and boot support; do not invent extra mount forelegs or flexible horns.
Original GLB positions, indices, material assignments, UVs, source cameras and approved source images remain immutable. Runtime deformation must clone geometry before writing.
Each mesh has one owner; a connected anatomy mesh cannot be attached to two independent rigid joints. Use explicit continuous weights on a runtime clone, or author a separate reviewed rig.
Locomotion never triggers attack, damage, armor shedding, spell, drum impact or death events automatically. Those require separate gameplay event channels.
Rest and reset must exactly restore working-copy positions and joint transforms. No accumulating per-frame rotations or vertex offsets.
Short rider legs and bent knees remain forward of the wing roots. Verify the collar/support path underneath the neck in side and underside views.
The rider hand, held grip and weapon remain a single owned chain; reins require constrained endpoints or a documented rest-preserving prototype.
reviewChecklist: Approve heavy lift, horn and knee clearance, seated support and the complete axe silhouette from oblique views.
Inspect front, both sides, rear and three-quarter motion at quarter-cycle intervals and at full speed.
Check every support contact or wing root, every held grip, and the complete follower assembly; no floating cuffs, armor, cargo or saddle.
Check loop position AND velocity, start/stop blend, turning ownership and reset after arbitrary scrubbing.
Check silhouette, self-intersection, membrane/tissue compression, foot sliding and ground penetration. A moving preview is not geometry/contact acceptance.
Compare current part inventory against the recorded GLB before admitting any new semantic binding.

models.name: Orc Dual-Seal Inquisitors
models.appearance: A green orc wears a tall split hood, gold-edged robes and shoulder skull tags, carrying a narrow shield and seal staff.

implementation.previewTimeEvaluation: Pure time/mode/speed/blend evaluation. Same phase gives the same pose after arbitrary seeking and reset; production start/stop envelopes remain pending.

gameplayAuthority.rule: Keep this route speed authoritative; preview cycle duration does not change gameplay velocity.

models.primaryMotion: Use an upright measured march, expressing authority through planted feet and controlled equipment rather than supernatural floating.
models.walk: Alternate heel placement and modest knee lift. Divide the robe around the advancing leg and shift hips over the supporting foot; staff stays nearly vertical.
models.run: Use a purposeful compact advance with forward torso inclination. Limit arm swing because both hands carry equipment; keep foot recovery clear beneath the robe.

cycle.phaseConvention: Normalized 0..1; time in seconds; all numeric amplitudes are initial review proposals.

phaseEvents.description: Left support begins; right heel releases.
Weight passes over the left support polygon.
Right leg clears the ground; left leg carries the body.
Right support begins; left heel releases.
Left recovery clears the ground.
Return to the left support event without a pose discontinuity.

cycle.strideAndLift: Propose total foot travel 0.22–0.34 of hip-to-sole length; recovery lift 0.06–0.10 of that length. Short legs use the lower range. Review against approved silhouette.
cycle.cadenceRule: Keep current data route speed 2.05; derive cadence from displacement. Try opposing leg phases half a cycle apart, roughly two-thirds walk stance, with a small tag delay after contact.
cycle.runRule: Separate final run/canter/flight-acceleration clips are required. Initial speed preview can adjust cadence but cannot claim completed run mechanics.

models.massAndBalance: Transfer the pelvis over the planted sole before lift. Keep the loaded hand and torso counterrotation smaller than the free arm. Heavy gear increases support time rather than adding a generic bounce.

partOwnership.coordinateFrame: Imported glTF scene: +Y up, +Z model front, X lateral. Bounds below are literal glTF accessor coordinates.
partOwnership.method: Literal mesh inventory and conservative name-based ownership review. Fused anatomy is recorded explicitly and is not split by names.

models.turning: Take short steps around a supporting leg, with head anticipation and limited chest twist. Keep the staff tip outside the feet.

transitions.authoredIntent: Acceleration starts at the hips, with the torso following the first planted step. Stops establish both feet before the heavy shoulders settle.
transitions.start: Blend from exact rest over a reviewable 0.15–0.30 second interval. Select a valid first support or wing phase before translating along the route.
transitions.stop: Keep the last support foot or carried saddle relationship; finish one restrained settle. Final route-aware support selection is not implemented in the START pilot.
transitions.turn: Yaw the route carrier separately from limb joints. Use the authored turning intent and replant/ bank only after endpoint and collision review.
transitions.scrubAndReset: Evaluate from rest coordinates at every frame; no cumulative integration. Test zero time, reverse scrubbing and repeated enable/disable.

models.secondaryMotion: The internal lantern may move slightly within its suspension. Cloth lags more than ribs; illumination remains separate from locomotion and is not a footfall-triggered effect.
eventConstraints: Preserve the lantern inside the chest, never under the chin. White rib prisms remain coherent rigid segments. Future spine controls must distribute bend around the cavity without crushing it, stretching rib roots or separating the staff grip.
Original GLB positions, indices, material assignments, UVs, source cameras and approved source images remain immutable. Runtime deformation must clone geometry before writing.
Each mesh has one owner; a connected anatomy mesh cannot be attached to two independent rigid joints. Use explicit continuous weights on a runtime clone, or author a separate reviewed rig.
Locomotion never triggers attack, damage, armor shedding, spell, drum impact or death events automatically. Those require separate gameplay event channels.
Rest and reset must exactly restore working-copy positions and joint transforms. No accumulating per-frame rotations or vertex offsets.
Contact events are proposed per support phase; route velocity stays authoritative. Match stride/cadence to displacement before enabling in-game root motion.
reviewChecklist: Review broad planted soles, chest clearance, staff balance and bounded lantern movement through walking and turning.
Inspect front, both sides, rear and three-quarter motion at quarter-cycle intervals and at full speed.
Check every support contact or wing root, every held grip, and the complete follower assembly; no floating cuffs, armor, cargo or saddle.
Check loop position AND velocity, start/stop blend, turning ownership and reset after arbitrary scrubbing.
Check silhouette, self-intersection, membrane/tissue compression, foot sliding and ground penetration. A moving preview is not geometry/contact acceptance.

models.appearance: A narrow dark bat carries a hooded goblin with dagger, two triangular scarves, gold purses and small bells, lighter in silhouette than the lancer.

implementation.previewTimeEvaluation: Pure time/mode/speed/blend evaluation. Same phase gives the same pose after arbitrary seeking and reset; production start/stop envelopes remain pending.

models.primaryMotion: Use agile readable flight with a quiet central body, controlled recovery and an anticipatory but supported rider posture.
models.flight: Drive shoulders into a compact downstroke, recovering through elbows and outer supports. Alternate active beats with short level glides. Keep compact rider knees ahead of wing roots, rather than spread around the bat's shoulders.

cycle.phaseConvention: Normalized 0..1; time in seconds; all numeric amplitudes are initial review proposals.

phaseEvents.description: Shoulder reaches the upper reversal; avoid an instantaneous direction snap.
Broad downstroke accelerates from shoulder through elbow.
Lower reversal; distal fingers lag the shoulder.
Recovery upstroke slightly folds the outer field.
Shoulder opens toward the next downstroke.
Wing position and velocity loop continuously.

cycle.strideAndLift: No ground stride in the primary flight clip. Initial shoulder stroke 18–30 degrees total around the actual lateral joint; elbow/finger response 5–12 degrees after 0.06–0.10 cycle. These are review proposals, not aerodynamic measurements.
cycle.cadenceRule: Keep current data route speed 2.50; derive cadence from displacement. Use fairly even beats with occasional gliding pauses; heavy purses lag farther in phase but less in amplitude than scarves.
cycle.runRule: Separate final run/canter/flight-acceleration clips are required. Initial speed preview can adjust cadence but cannot claim completed run mechanics.

models.massAndBalance: The biological trunk carries saddle and rider. Wing force produces restrained trunk response; rider hips remain seated and short bent knees stay forward of the wing roots. Collar support remains underneath the neck, never on top of the head.

models.turning: Start with a head glance and bank. Scarves and purses trail outside while the rider stays seated and the dagger avoids the reins.

transitions.authoredIntent: Lean the bat forward before increasing stroke reach. Braking levels the body before damping rider lean and loose accessories, rather than halting everything together.
transitions.start: Blend from exact rest over a reviewable 0.15–0.30 second interval. Select a valid first support or wing phase before translating along the route.
transitions.stop: Keep the last support foot or carried saddle relationship; finish one restrained settle. Final route-aware support selection is not implemented in the START pilot.
transitions.turn: Yaw the route carrier separately from limb joints. Use the authored turning intent and replant/ bank only after endpoint and collision review.
transitions.scrubAndReset: Evaluate from rest coordinates at every frame; no cumulative integration. Test zero time, reverse scrubbing and repeated enable/disable.

models.secondaryMotion: Scarves have greater tip lag than heavy purses; bells rotate only slightly at their attachments. Their motion must not automatically signal an ability.
eventConstraints: Future controls preserve lower-neck collar, supported rein ends, short legs, dagger grip and every accessory root. Check membrane clearance from scarves at maximum bank and recovery. Do not reuse the long-lance pose from host_42 or introduce extra wings to support its equipment.

Each mesh has one owner; a connected anatomy mesh cannot be attached to two independent rigid joints. Use explicit continuous weights on a runtime clone, or author a separate reviewed rig.
Locomotion never triggers attack, damage, armor shedding, spell, drum impact or death events automatically. Those require separate gameplay event channels.
Rest and reset must exactly restore working-copy positions and joint transforms. No accumulating per-frame rotations or vertex offsets.
Short rider legs and bent knees remain forward of the wing roots. Verify the collar/support path underneath the neck in side and underside views.
The rider hand, held grip and weapon remain a single owned chain; reins require constrained endpoints or a documented rest-preserving prototype.
reviewChecklist: Approve compact seating, separate accessories and sharp wing mechanics without uncontrolled flutter.
Inspect front, both sides, rear and three-quarter motion at quarter-cycle intervals and at full speed.
Check every support contact or wing root, every held grip, and the complete follower assembly; no floating cuffs, armor, cargo or saddle.
Check loop position AND velocity, start/stop blend, turning ownership and reset after arbitrary scrubbing.
Check silhouette, self-intersection, membrane/tissue compression, foot sliding and ground penetration. A moving preview is not geometry/contact acceptance.

models.primaryMotion: Use commanding heavy flight with a stable throne and clear wing articulation, emphasizing scale without changing authoritative gameplay travel speed.
models.flight: Drive two wing forelimbs through shoulders, elbows and distal supports, with strong downstroke and longer recovery. Neck and tail balance the throne's mass. The rider absorbs lift through seated hips and attached stirrups, never bouncing independently above the seat.

cycle.phaseConvention: Normalized 0..1; time in seconds; all numeric amplitudes are initial review proposals.

phaseEvents.description: Both forewing shoulders approach the upper reversal.
Heavy power stroke accelerates from the shoulders.
Outer fingers finish the power stroke after the root.
Recovery folds the distal field slightly.
The broad membrane reopens for the next stroke.
Full wing and tail pose loops continuously.

cycle.strideAndLift: No primary ground stride. Initial shoulder stroke 18–28 degrees total; distal fold 5–10 degrees delayed by 0.07–0.11 cycle. Preserve TWO hindlegs and TWO wing forelimbs, never a separate extra pair of forelegs.

cycle.runRule: Separate final run/canter/flight-acceleration clips are required. Initial speed preview can adjust cadence but cannot claim completed run mechanics.

models.massAndBalance: Large biological torso and long neck carry a heavy rider/throne load. Shoulders drive the stroke; head stabilizes with small delayed neck response, and the tail counterbalances. Rider, seat, reins and chains require ownership under the carried mass.

models.turning: Use wide deliberate banks. Neck anticipates travel, tail counters roll, and the firmly carried throne supports the rider's small lean.

transitions.authoredIntent: Brace both hind feet before takeoff. Landing places them beneath the combined mass, then settles neck, throne and rider in sequence.
transitions.start: Blend from exact rest over a reviewable 0.15–0.30 second interval. Select a valid first support or wing phase before translating along the route.
transitions.stop: Keep the last support foot or carried saddle relationship; finish one restrained settle. Final route-aware support selection is not implemented in the START pilot.
transitions.turn: Yaw the route carrier separately from limb joints. Use the authored turning intent and replant/ bank only after endpoint and collision review.
transitions.scrubAndReset: Evaluate from rest coordinates at every frame; no cumulative integration. Test zero time, reverse scrubbing and repeated enable/disable.

models.secondaryMotion: Robes and rein slack trail acceleration. Sword aura remains separate from locomotion; the right weapon hand never swaps roles with the left rein hand.
eventConstraints: Preserve two hind legs, two wing forelimbs, one rider and an obscured face. Future controls retain throne, stirrup and lower-neck support. No extra forelegs, orange accents or face reveal. Use approved catalog identity, despite older gameplay naming and unused variant descriptions in data.
Original GLB positions, indices, material assignments, UVs, source cameras and approved source images remain immutable. Runtime deformation must clone geometry before writing.
Each mesh has one owner; a connected anatomy mesh cannot be attached to two independent rigid joints. Use explicit continuous weights on a runtime clone, or author a separate reviewed rig.
Locomotion never triggers attack, damage, armor shedding, spell, drum impact or death events automatically. Those require separate gameplay event channels.
Rest and reset must exactly restore working-copy positions and joint transforms. No accumulating per-frame rotations or vertex offsets.
Short rider legs and bent knees remain forward of the wing roots. Verify the collar/support path underneath the neck in side and underside views.
The rider hand, held grip and weapon remain a single owned chain; reins require constrained endpoints or a documented rest-preserving prototype.

Approved identity is Lord Bernhard; gameplay data still contains an older name/description. Keep the hidden face, right sword, left reins and near-black/crimson appearance. Do not revive the orange staff or unused legacy variants.

phaseEvents.description: Shoulder reaches the upper reversal; avoid an instantaneous direction snap.

cycle.runRule: Separate final run/canter/flight-acceleration clips are required. Initial speed preview can adjust cadence but cannot claim completed run mechanics.

transitions.authoredIntent: Start through hip transfer and a gentle lean. Stops plant both feet, then settle shoulders, hands and the two carried sacs in order.
transitions.start: Blend from exact rest over a reviewable 0.15–0.30 second interval. Select a valid first support or wing phase before translating along the route.
transitions.stop: Keep the last support foot or carried saddle relationship; finish one restrained settle. Final route-aware support selection is not implemented in the START pilot.
transitions.turn: Yaw the route carrier separately from limb joints. Use the authored turning intent and replant/ bank only after endpoint and collision review.
transitions.scrubAndReset: Evaluate from rest coordinates at every frame; no cumulative integration. Test zero time, reverse scrubbing and repeated enable/disable.

models.secondaryMotion: Sacs sway independently within bindings but deform less than cloth. Regeneration pulses belong to their established event, never every footfall.
eventConstraints: Future controls preserve two connected fists and thumbs, sack neck support, central harness and actual boots. Do not inherit rogue blades, cloak or mask. This inferred variant has different body anatomy, not just another palette. Check sac clearance from upper arms and head throughout a turn.
Original GLB positions, indices, material assignments, UVs, source cameras and approved source images remain immutable. Runtime deformation must clone geometry before writing.
Each mesh has one owner; a connected anatomy mesh cannot be attached to two independent rigid joints. Use explicit continuous weights on a runtime clone, or author a separate reviewed rig.
Locomotion never triggers attack, damage, armor shedding, spell, drum impact or death events automatically. Those require separate gameplay event channels.
Rest and reset must exactly restore working-copy positions and joint transforms. No accumulating per-frame rotations or vertex offsets.
Contact events are proposed per support phase; route velocity stays authoritative. Match stride/cadence to displacement before enabling in-game root motion.
reviewChecklist: Approve sack support, long-arm clearance, planted feet and the distinct pale troll silhouette.
Inspect front, both sides, rear and three-quarter motion at quarter-cycle intervals and at full speed.
Check every support contact or wing root, every held grip, and the complete follower assembly; no floating cuffs, armor, cargo or saddle.
Check loop position AND velocity, start/stop blend, turning ownership and reset after arbitrary scrubbing.
Check silhouette, self-intersection, membrane/tissue compression, foot sliding and ground penetration. A moving preview is not geometry/contact acceptance.
Compare current part inventory against the recorded GLB before admitting any new semantic binding.
